correctness.rationale: For a normal diagonal operator the squared norm is the maximum of cos²(t) and r²cos²(t-φ),r²cos²(t-ψ) integrated over the projective circle. Strict decreasing rearrangement bounds each winner cell integral by (ell+sin ell)/2. At fixed strong length L, strict sine concavity sets weak lengths equal and leaves strictly concave scalar G_r(L) with unique maximizer L=pi-4asin(r/2). The proposed phases +/- (pi/2-asin(r/2)) realize all centered winner arcs, and equality in rearrangement plus strict concavity fixes phase classes up to weak exchange. Taylor substitution gives cubic and quintic coefficients. Independent direct angular quadrature at r=.1,.3,.7,1 agrees with the formula, and symbolic expansion matches. At r=1 the equal-modulus unitary endpoint is consistent; r=0 excluded because phase equality would cease to be unique. No independent-modulus or nonnormal claim.
